chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about the sa'ibah. He said:
Look in the Qur'an: whatever in it contains the freeing of a slave, that, O Ammar, is the sa'ibah, who has no wala' belonging to any of the Muslims over him except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

So whatever wala' belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then it is for His Messenger; and whatever is for His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, then indeed its wala' is for the Imam. His liability for offense is upon the Imam, and his inheritance belongs to him.

key_terms.جِنَايَتَهُ: his legal liability for offense or wrongdoing
key_terms.وَلَاءَ: the bond of allegiance, legal affiliation, and authority connected to a freed person
key_terms.ٱلسَّائِبَةِ: a freed person released without personal wala' affiliation to a specific individual
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the Imam who holds the legal wala' after the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the wala' and inheritance of a sa'ibah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal status of the sa'ibah, a freed person whose wala' is not attached to any ordinary Muslim. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام links this ruling to the Qur'anic references to freeing slaves and states that such wala' ultimately belongs to Allah عزّ وجلّ, then to His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and then to the Imam. The hadith also establishes that the Imam bears the legal responsibility connected to this person and receives his inheritance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3504 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ammar ibn Abi Al-Ahwas, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), about al-sa'ibah (a freed slave without specific ties).

Imam (as) said: "Look in the Qur'an. Wherever there is mention of the freeing of a slave, that, O Ammar, refers to the sa'ibah, who has no wala' (loyalty) to any Muslim except Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic.

So, whoever's wala' belongs to Allah (swt), it belongs to His Messenger.
And whatever belongs to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, its wala' belongs to the Imam.
His liabilities (for crimes or debts) are upon the Imam, and his inheritance belongs to the Imam."
